key_findings.finding: Direct evidence exists in a murine therapeutic model: α-galactosylceramide-loaded CD1d–anti-HER2 fusion protein (iNKT/CD1d-antitumor therapy) was combined with OVA peptide/CpG vaccination against established B16 melanoma expressing HER2 and OVA. The combination optimized NK and OVA-specific CD8 responses, increased inflammatory DC/serum IL-12 responses, and produced greater tumor inhibition than the vaccine or immunotherapy components alone; depletion experiments indicated that enhanced tumor control depended mainly on CTLs rather than NK cells. The abstract establishes significance qualitatively, but the retrieved passages do not provide exact tumor-volume values, survival curves, or p-values.

key_findings.finding: A second direct murine combination study used α-GalCer plus CpG and melanoma peptides (Melan-A:26 and gp100:44), delivered in a multicomponent nanoparticle, in B16F10 melanoma. The combination restrained tumor growth; tumor volume was reported as approximately fivefold lower than with otherwise similar nanoparticles lacking GalCer. GalCer-loaded nanoparticles enhanced intratumoral NKT/NK infiltration and cytokine responses, while soluble GalCer mixed with peptide/TLR ligands achieved similar tumor control, so the antitumor benefit supports the combination but not necessarily nanoparticle-specific superiority. No survival endpoint or exact p-value was available in the retrieved abstract/full-text extract.

key_findings.finding: A related direct peptide-vaccine study in C57BL/6J mice with established HPV genital/TC-1 tumors used intranasal HPV E6/E7 peptides plus α-GalCer and CpG-ODN (TVAC).
